leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members prefer B041 as a single-part prize for Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. All five describe the core as Katori's magic-wavelength lattice, which removes the light shift so that many atoms can be interrogated at once, plus the realisation at the 10^-18 level, and all five stress independent reproduction and comparison across laboratories. Their citations differ: Johansson's mentions opening new tests of fundamental physics, Kroll's and Olsson's name magic-wavelength trapping, and Lindroth's names the 10^-18 level. They do not share one view of what the discovery is. Several treat the fundamental-physics payoff as still prospective, and Johansson and Lindroth say the citation should lead with the clocks themselves. Kroll, Olsson and Lindroth want the citation to name the lattice concept. Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth also raise the contributions of Lemonde, Takamoto, Derevianko and the NIST, PTB and SYRTE groups, which a two-name prize cannot cover.

Danielsson alone prefers B004 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) as the discovery with the clearest before and after, citing the Z2 invariant, protected HgTe edge transport and fifteen years of confirmation. He concedes that the 2016 topological prize is close and that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and Hasan are outside the three names. Eriksson, Lindroth and Olsson mention B004 or its attribution, but only Eriksson and Lindroth list it as an alternative.

Eriksson alone prefers B017, with a three-name credit (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) that he widened from his opening two-name pair. His case is a theory-then-experiment pairing that independent groups have reproduced. He accepts that the pairing mechanism is unresolved and that his own weight on maturity may be too generous, and says optical lattice clocks have unquestionable maturity. Mehlig lists B017 as an alternative while calling it premature.

Mehlig alone prefers B027 (Young, Halperin, Nelson) as a mature, analytically controlled theory with clean authorship of the decisive papers. He acknowledges the overlap with the 2016 prize, first-order melting in some real systems, and that no other member's round-1 file prefers it. He lists B041 as his first alternative and says he would accept it as the likely consensus.

areas_of_agreement: Five of eight members explicitly prefer B041 (Katori and Ye) as their round-1 single-part configuration, and Mehlig and Danielsson each list B041 among their alternatives, as does Eriksson. No member's file argues that B041 lacks the maturity, independent reproduction or credit clarity for the two named people.

Members who comment on attribution agree that the two names Katori and Ye are clean for the lattice-clock concept and its record-level realisation, though several caution that others made essential contributions to accuracy evaluation.

Most members state that the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes are distinct from the lattice clock but that the citation must separate them. Kroll, Olsson, Mehlig and Lindroth each ask that the citation rest on magic-wavelength lattice trapping.

Members who discuss B028 (circuit QED) agree it is foundational and widely reproduced, and no one disputes its merit. Eriksson, Lindroth, Kroll, Olsson and Johansson each raise timing relative to the 2025 prize and/or the four-name credit problem.
Members who discuss attribution in B029 (IceCube) agree it is a genuine new window and that credit within a large collaboration is hard to cut to two or three names.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a discovery or a measurement refinement: Danielsson and Eriksson say the discovery content lies in instrumentation and the fundamental-physics payoff is mostly promised, while Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Johansson argue it opens a new regime (many-body clock physics, millimetre-scale redshift, geodesy, constant tests). Johansson and Lindroth note that constant-variation results are so far null.

Whether the 2016 topological prize overlaps B004 (Danielsson says no, since time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulators need no magnetic field; Mehlig says the Z2 idea is a direct extension) and B027 (Mehlig concedes overlap; Danielsson and Eriksson see it as a real obstacle).

Whether an unresolved pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene should delay recognition of B017: Eriksson says the cited discovery is the existence of the correlated phases, not their origin, and cites high-Tc superconductors; Danielsson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Johansson say the interpretation is still moving.

Whether the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits makes B028 premature or duplicative: Eriksson and Lindroth say yes; Kroll says the subject differs (coupling to photons versus tunnelling).

Whether TXS 0506+056 at roughly three sigma and the newer Galactic-plane and NGC 1068 results make IceCube (B029) mature enough, versus a solid diffuse-flux discovery with astronomy still being built.

How the committee weighs a purely theoretical statistical-physics result (B027) and theory-led enabling proposals (B002, which Lindroth ranked second and Johansson sixth) against instrument and measurement discoveries.
attribution_disputes: B041: Katori and Ye are accepted as the core pair, but Lemonde, Takamoto, Derevianko, Ludlow, Gill and the NIST, PTB and SYRTE groups are named as having contributed to the concept or its accuracy evaluation. Johansson wants the citation to name the concept and first record-level realisations so as not to invite a priority argument.

B004: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe realisation behind Molenkamp's experiment, and Hasan, Fu, Moore and Balents are tied to the 3D case. Danielsson, Eriksson, Olsson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce each flag this. Only Danielsson prefers B004, and he concedes the point.

B017: all three names appear in Eriksson's configuration, Bistritzer in addition to MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero. Eriksson says Olsson, Johansson and Mehlig influenced him toward Bistritzer. Eriksson also notes that Cao, Dean, Young, Yazdani and Efetov have claims. Mehlig would be more comfortable if the citation were restricted to flat bands and correlated insulators.
B028: the four-name list forces an exclusion, and Eriksson, Kroll and Olsson each resolve it differently. Olsson and Johansson say that excluding Blais, who led the 2004 proposal, is hard to defend.

B029 and B011: Pearce and Kroll say a roughly 300-person collaboration offers no defensible cut at three names, and that B011 without van Paradijs looks incomplete. Mehlig notes that B027 is cleaner by comparison.
B034: Kroll notes that the trio is contested (Chu absent; Mlynek, Keith and Bordé overlaps), and Lindroth also calls the credit messy.
maturity_disputes: B017 is eight years from the 2018 experiments. Danielsson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Johansson raise prematurity, while Eriksson cites independent reproduction and fractional Chern insulators in moire systems as evidence of lasting impact.

B041's maturity is not contested for the clock itself, but Kroll, Eriksson and Danielsson note that the 10^-18 figures, the redefinition of the second and the fundamental-physics payoffs are not complete.
B029: the TXS 0506+056 evidence is roughly three sigma, and the Galactic-plane and NGC 1068 results are recent.
B027 is regarded as mature in interpretation by Mehlig, but Danielsson and Eriksson say experimental confirmation is less decisive, with first-order melting in some systems.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (johansson-goran) discloses leading the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and working closely with superconducting-qubit groups at Chalmers, adjacent to the B028 candidates. He says he may need to recuse himself or discount his opening B028 ranking. Eriksson suggests he not lead the discussion of B028, Kroll says his B028 support should be counted accordingly (recusal), and Lindroth says it is right that he weigh how much to push it himself.

Kroll (kroll-stefan) discloses a visit during his PhD to John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, within the JILA environment of Ye, with no collaboration with Katori or Ye. He does not consider it grounds for recusal. He also notes that his WACQT role touches the Chalmers community relevant to B028.

Lindroth (lindroth-eva) discloses a long collaboration with Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and Lund and ETH attosecond groups, with no tie to B041 names. She suggests that the committee secretary confirm that no recusal is needed for B002, B034 and B042.
Eriksson (eriksson-olle) notes that he chaired the committee for the 2025 prize, which bears on the timing argument about B028. He reports no tie to any credited candidate.
Olsson (olsson-eva) and Mehlig (mehlig-bernhard) disclose that they share the Chalmers environment with Johansson, with no specific collaboration found.

Pearce (pearce-mark, chair) works in the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations and the same astroparticle community as B029 and B011, with no tie to the credited individuals. Pearce is a B041 supporter and treats his own ranking as one view of eight.
questions_for_round2: For B041: can the committee agree a citation that names magic-wavelength lattice trapping and Katori's and Ye's realisations, separating it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes without implying that NIST, PTB, SYRTE and others made no contribution?

For B041: do Danielsson and Eriksson accept the lattice clock as prize-worthy discovery-grade physics, or is their reservation (new quantum behaviour versus better measurement) a reason to oppose it? Is a precision-measurement prize acceptable this year?

For B004: can anyone name a defensible three-person set that handles Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Hasan, and is the 2016 topology prize judged to cover Z2 topological insulators? If not, would Danielsson move toward B041, or is a different B004 trio possible?

For B017: do Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson treat an unresolved pairing mechanism as disqualifying, or would a citation limited to flat bands and correlated insulators with Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero suffice? Do the condensed-matter members regard the core discovery as stable?
For B027: do members other than Mehlig see evidence that the hexatic phase was confirmed experimentally and that the 2016 citation did not cover it, as Mehlig is asked to show?
For B028: how should Johansson's disclosed proximity be handled (recusal, discounting of his support, or participation in technical points), and does the 2025 prize bar B028 this year?
For B029 and B011: can any member propose a two- or three-name credit for IceCube or GRB afterglows that is defensible, given the collaboration size and the van Paradijs omission?

Is any two-part configuration viable? Johansson notes that a second part would push the union above three people, and Kroll rejects B034 as a second part. Is a single B041 prize the only configuration within the name limit?
summary.chair_observation: Five of the eight round-1 files prefer B041 alone, while B004, B017 and B027 each have one explicit supporter and no member's file prefers any other ballot. The B041 members agree on the pair of names and on the evidence of reproduction, while the dissenters' reservations concern novelty relative to 2005 and 2012 and whether the fundamental-physics payoff is delivered. The single-supporter positions each face a specific attribution or maturity objection that their own proponents acknowledge, and those objections, and the citation wording for B041, are the main points for round 2. This summary counts only explicit round-1 configurations and statements, and not hidden votes.
